transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Well, I'm here because for the past year or so, I just feel like I’m always puttering around. I'm constantly fixing things, arranging, or volunteering for just one more thing. You'd think I'd be slowing down, but even at 87, I just have a really hard time sitting down and being still.
Have you been needing less sleep than usual?
No, I wouldn't say that. I still sleep about the same amount I always have. I just... when I'm awake, I can't seem to stop moving. But my sleep hasn't changed.
Do you feel driven to keep busy because you’re worrying a lot?

No, I don't think so. I'm not really a worrier, to be honest. It's not like I have a lot on my mind that's making me anxious or anything like that. It's more of just a physical urge to keep moving. I don't feel worried at all, I just feel restless if my hands aren't busy doing something.
During these times when you can't stop moving, do you also feel unusually cheerful or energized compared with your normal self?

No, not really. I don't feel unusually cheerful or, you know, overly energized like I could take on the world. I feel like myself, just... myself who can't seem to sit still. My mood is completely normal.
Do unwanted thoughts keep popping into your mind and make you feel like you have to do these activities to relieve them?

No, nothing like that. I don't have unwanted thoughts popping into my head, and I'm not doing things to try and relieve them. It really is just... well, my hands just want to keep busy. It doesn't have anything to do with my thoughts.
Did this restlessness start after you began a new medication or changed the dose of one?
No, I haven't started any new medications recently, and my doses haven't changed either. I've been on the same prescriptions for a good while now.
Have you been like this since you were young?

Yes, it's been like this for as long as I can remember. Even back in grade school, I was always getting scolded for popping out of my seat or talking over my classmates. The teachers were always telling my parents I was just... too lively. So, yes, it's been this way long before I was even a teenager.
